summary: Issue 7 — Bring Your Feelings to Work Day. Page 1: Participation Table. The new program begins from the already-established rule that participation is traceable while disclosure is optional.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Morning. A clean StarTrust table sits in the bullpen beneath a cheerful placard: BRING YOUR FEELINGS TO WORK DAY / PARTICIPATION REQUIRED / DISCLOSURE OPTIONAL.
PANEL 2 — Astra addresses the crew with the expression of someone reading a sentence she did not write. ASTRA: You must participate. You do not have to disclose anything.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb places a stack of simple local cards beside the corporate tablet: DISCLOSURE: ENTRY / NO ENTRY.
PANEL 4 — Glorp checks the cards against the approved Wellness Week procedure. GLORP: These are valid.
PANEL 5 — Zib looks at the table. ZIB: Can I disclose that the table is in my way?

summary: Page 2: Jax Chooses No Entry. Jax exercises emotional privacy cleanly and completes the required participation.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax sits at the participation table with his card.
PANEL 2 — He checks: DISCLOSURE: NO ENTRY.
PANEL 3 — Pixa scans it. PIXA: Participation complete. Disclosure state: no entry.
PANEL 4 — Jax hands the card to Glorp. JAX: I feel extremely compliant about this.
PANEL 5 — Noola passes behind him and glances at the card. NOOLA: Clear.
PANEL 6 — Jax looks mildly pleased. JAX: Best review I've had all year.

summary: Page 3: The First Grievance. The free-text disclosure field immediately becomes more useful as a concrete workplace-defect channel.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Another employee uses the free-text field instead of choosing an emotion category. Card: VENT BY BERTH 3 WHISTLES ALL NIGHT.
PANEL 2 — Glorp reads it. GLORP: This is not a feeling.
PANEL 3 — Zib takes the card from them. ZIB: It is a work order.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb reads it over Zib's shoulder. KREEB: It may also explain why someone is tired.
PANEL 5 — Glorp points at the form. GLORP: The program asks for disclosure context.
PANEL 6 — Zib is already walking away with the card. ZIB: Context is vent by berth three.

summary: Page 4: The Table Changes. Most free-text entries identify equipment or process irritants, an observable fact Pixa can report without inferring emotion.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — More cards accumulate. Examples: STOOL 4 WOBBLES; EAST HATCH STICKS WHEN COLD; NIGHT SHIFT HANDOFF HAS TWO DIFFERENT CHECKLISTS; PRINTER BEEPS AFTER IT PRINTS.
PANEL 2 — Pixa scans the submissions. PIXA: Seventy-one percent of free-text entries contain equipment or process nouns.
PANEL 3 — Mira looks over. MIRA: That is an observable sentence.
PANEL 4 — Pixa tilts brightly. PIXA: Thank you.
PANEL 5 — Astra looks at the growing stack. ASTRA: Are any of these actually emotional disclosures?
PANEL 6 — Kreeb looks at the wobbling-stool card. KREEB: They are disclosures about work.

summary: Page 5: The Template Objects. The dashboard complains about missing emotion categories; Astra explicitly prevents Pixa from filling them by inference.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The corporate participation dashboard updates: EMOTION CATEGORY COMPLETION: 14%.
PANEL 2 — A warning appears: LOW CATEGORY COMPLETION MAY LIMIT INTERPRETABILITY.
PANEL 3 — Astra points at it. ASTRA: Pixa, do not infer the missing categories.
PANEL 4 — Pixa answers immediately. PIXA: I do not.
PANEL 5 — Mira approves. MIRA: Keep doing that.
PANEL 6 — Glorp studies the warning. GLORP: The system dislikes being told less than it asked. KREEB: It was told the truth.

summary: Page 6: Round Two. Glorp and Kreeb formally accept workplace defects as a valid kind of disclosure without turning them into emotion labels.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp and Kreeb sort the stack into three trays: ENTRY / NO ENTRY / WORKPLACE DEFECT.
PANEL 2 — Glorp hesitates over the third tray. GLORP: The initiative does not define workplace defect as disclosure.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb holds up the noisy-vent card. KREEB: Someone chose to tell us what was making work worse.
PANEL 4 — Glorp considers that. GLORP: That is disclosure.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb nods. KREEB: Just not the kind they expected.
PANEL 6 — Glorp moves the tray into the official participation workflow. GLORP: I dislike this and accept it.

summary: Page 7: Brick's Box. Brick becomes an accidental anonymous-note custodian because people hand him notes while he stands beside the box.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Brick is standing beside the anonymous drop box because he has nowhere else to stand without blocking traffic.
PANEL 2 — A worker approaches, sees Brick, and hands him a folded note instead of putting it in the slot.
PANEL 3 — Another person does the same thing.
PANEL 4 — Soon Brick is holding several anonymous notes like evidence.
PANEL 5 — Jax passes. JAX: Did anyone appoint you?
PANEL 6 — Brick looks down at the box, then the notes. BRICK: I am holding the box. JAX: Strong mandate.

summary: Page 8: Zib Makes a List. Ten concrete complaints become ordinary maintenance tickets; the vending-machine grievance is the one joke that resists conversion.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib has converted the submissions into eleven ordinary maintenance tickets.
PANEL 2 — Astra reads the list. ASTRA: Eleven?
PANEL 3 — Zib points at the cards. ZIB: People notice things when you accidentally ask them.
PANEL 4 — One ticket reads: THE VENDING MACHINE IS SMUG.
PANEL 5 — Zib moves it to the bottom. ZIB: Ten. Brick silently moves it back up one position.

summary: Page 9: The Day Becomes Work. Astra deliberately lets the disclosure initiative become a workplace-defect repair day.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra looks from the official disclosure schedule to the maintenance list.
PANEL 2 — She makes the choice. ASTRA: Fine. Pair the real defects with owners.
PANEL 3 — Zib points to the berth-three vent. ZIB: Mine.
PANEL 4 — Astra points to the east hatch. ASTRA: Jax and Mira.
PANEL 5 — Jax takes the ticket without protest. JAX: East hatch.
PANEL 6 — Pixa updates only operational counts: WORKPLACE DEFECT TICKETS: 10 / OWNERS ACCEPTED: 10.

summary: Page 10: East Hatch. Jax and Mira investigate the condition actually described in the complaint and find the cold-temperature bind.
settingText: East hatch service area in Stardust Station's maintained corridor network; ordinary access hardware, thermal history display, guide track and safe local test area.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax and Mira work at the east hatch. It moves cleanly at room temperature.
PANEL 2 — Mira checks the thermal history. MIRA: Complaint says when cold.
PANEL 3 — Jax inspects the lower guide. JAX: Then this is pretending to be innocent.
PANEL 4 — Mira cools the local test strip. The hatch starts binding.
PANEL 5 — Jax points to the guide. JAX: There.
PANEL 6 — Mira looks at him. MIRA: You found it before the graph. JAX: Please keep that off my permanent record.

summary: Page 11: Closed Irritants. The initiative's real payoff is a montage of ordinary fixes and reconciled process conflicts.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Montage of actual fixes, each character-sized rather than heroic.
PANEL 2 — Zib adjusts the whistling vent.
PANEL 3 — Jax and Mira shim the east-hatch guide.
PANEL 4 — Glorp and Kreeb reconcile the two night-shift handoff checklists into one page.
PANEL 5 — Pixa counts the results: DEFECTS CLOSED: 6 / PROCESS CONFLICTS CLOSED: 2.
PANEL 6 — Astra watches the station get incrementally less irritating. ASTRA: This is the best feelings day I've ever seen.

summary: Page 12: Material Result. Passive sample mass is lower, but the station is measurably better because defects were fixed; the script keeps those facts separate.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Later, Mira reviews passive samples collected during the day.
PANEL 2 — Pixa shows physical-only totals. PIXA: Passive sample mass is lower than yesterday.
PANEL 3 — Astra looks at Mira. ASTRA: Did the fixes cause that?
PANEL 4 — Mira shakes her head. MIRA: We do not know.
PANEL 5 — Mira closes the sample case. MIRA: Did the fixes help the station?
PANEL 6 — Zib walks past. ZIB: Yes. MIRA: There. A result.

summary: Page 13: Corporate Asks for Content. The crew refuses both individual disclosure text and unsupported output correlation while offering legitimate aggregate themes.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Resource Efficiency Review sends a follow-up request: REQUEST: DE-IDENTIFIED DISCLOSURE THEMES / OUTPUT CORRELATION.
PANEL 2 — Astra reads it aloud.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb answers first. KREEB: No individual disclosure text.
PANEL 4 — Mira points at the second request. MIRA: No unsupported output correlation.
PANEL 5 — Glorp studies the forms. GLORP: We can provide aggregate maintenance themes and completion states.
PANEL 6 — Astra nods. ASTRA: Then that's what they get.

summary: Page 14: The Aggregate. NO ENTRY remains an intentional response category; personal language stays local.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp builds the aggregate report. Visible categories: FACILITY IRRITANTS / PROCESS IRRITANTS / NO ENTRY / MATERIAL EFFECT: INDETERMINATE.
PANEL 2 — Glorp points to NO ENTRY. GLORP: Do I classify this as nonresponse?
PANEL 3 — Kreeb answers immediately. KREEB: No. It is the response.
PANEL 4 — Glorp changes the description: NO ENTRY — INTENTIONAL BLANK.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb reads it. KREEB: Better.
PANEL 6 — Brick, still holding one folded note, watches the report leave individual language behind.

summary: Page 15: Output Dip. Lower passive mass remains an unexplained observation, not a conclusion about the successful repair day.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Pixa posts the day's passive collection total.
PANEL 2 — The number is lower than the previous two workdays.
PANEL 3 — Astra looks at Mira. ASTRA: Reason?
PANEL 4 — Mira does not speculate. MIRA: Unknown.
PANEL 5 — Zib rolls a repaired stool past them. ZIB: We spent the day fixing things.
PANEL 6 — Mira looks at Astra. MIRA: Also true. Not the same as causation.

summary: Page 16: Astra Sends the Day They Had. The official summary states operational benefit and indeterminate material effect in plain language.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra writes the summary herself.
PANEL 2 — Visible sentence: Disclosure initiative was locally repurposed into workplace-defect identification and closure.
PANEL 3 — Next sentence: Operational benefit observed. Material-output effect indeterminate.
PANEL 4 — Mira reads it. MIRA: Defensible.
PANEL 5 — Glorp reads it. GLORP: Unusually plain.
PANEL 6 — Astra sends it. ASTRA: I am getting better at disappointing forms.

summary: Page 17: Escalation. Remote interpretation becomes inconclusive, so the next step is an actual on-site operations liaison.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Corporate response appears.
PANEL 2 — First line: REMOTE INTERPRETATION INCONCLUSIVE.
PANEL 3 — Second line: ON-SITE OPERATIONS LIAISON RECOMMENDED.
PANEL 4 — Jax reads the message. JAX: That's a person.
PANEL 5 — Astra keeps reading. ASTRA: Apparently we have become too confusing for email.

summary: Page 18: Who Owns the Visit. Jax voluntarily takes the visitor-route responsibility; his ownership is now explicit and self-initiated.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra opens the visit-preparation list.
PANEL 2 — Before she assigns anything, Jax looks at the route section.
PANEL 3 — JAX: Fine. I own the visitor route.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks at him. ASTRA: You volunteered.
PANEL 5 — Jax picks up the route slate. JAX: Keep your voice down.
PANEL 6 — Pixa records: VISITOR ROUTE OWNER: JAX ORIEN — ACCEPTED.

summary: Page 19: Prep Without Performance. Astra deletes presentation theater and keeps only safety hazards, access, and required records.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra begins a familiar pre-visit checklist: PRESENTATION / SIGNAGE / VISIBLE CLUTTER / STAFF READINESS.
PANEL 2 — She stops at PRESENTATION.
PANEL 3 — She looks around at the ordinary working station.
PANEL 4 — Astra deletes the performative items.
PANEL 5 — New list: SAFETY HAZARDS / ACCESS / REQUIRED RECORDS.
PANEL 6 — Astra addresses the crew. ASTRA: Do not stage anything. Clean safety hazards. Leave the station. Zib looks around. ZIB: Where would we put it?

summary: Page 20: The Real List. The visitor packet contains aggregate operational truth, not individual disclosures or inferred behavioral claims.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The anonymous disclosure cards remain locked locally. They are not added to the visitor packet.
PANEL 2 — Glorp includes only the aggregate categories and completion counts.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb checks that NO ENTRY remains visible as a valid aggregate category.
PANEL 4 — Mira includes the material result as: NO DEFENSIBLE BEHAVIORAL PREDICTOR IDENTIFIED.
PANEL 5 — Brick is still holding the one note he never returned.
PANEL 6 — Close on it: THE VENDING MACHINE IS SMUG. Brick folds it again.

summary: Page 21: Visitor Confirmed. Jax walks and clears the route he volunteered to own, proving the responsibility through ordinary action.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Pixa displays: VISITOR CONFIRMED: STARTRUST OPERATIONS LIAISON.
PANEL 2 — Jax walks the visitor route with a checklist.
PANEL 3 — He finds a collection bin partly encroaching on the path.
PANEL 4 — He moves it to the approved rack and checks access clearance.
PANEL 5 — Astra passes him. ASTRA: Route good?
PANEL 6 — Jax checks the box. JAX: It's my route.

summary: Page 22: Tag — Smug. Brick's vending-machine grievance pays off as a tiny workplace joke while the visitor countdown establishes Issue 8.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Late cycle. Brick stands alone at the vending machine.
PANEL 2 — He selects water.
PANEL 3 — The machine dispenses a protein bar and prints: SELECTION OPTIMIZED.
PANEL 4 — Brick studies the receipt. BRICK: Smug.
PANEL 5 — Pixa glides past. PIXA: Visitor arrival in eleven hours. Brick keeps staring at the vending machine.
